# 4 Ezra Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — First dialogue

---

**1** Then the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered

**2** and said to me: Your heart has utterly failed in its understanding of this world, and do you think to comprehend the way of the Most High?

**3** Then I said: Yes, my lord. And he answered me and said: I have been sent to show you three ways and to set before you three riddles.

**4** If you can resolve one of these for me, I also will show you the way you desire to see, and will instruct you from where the evil heart proceeds.

**5** Then I said: Speak, my lord. And he said to me: Come, weigh for me the heaviness of fire; or measure for me a measure of wind; or recall for me a day that has passed.

**6** I answered and said: Who of those born of woman is able to do this, that you should ask me such things?

**7** And he said to me: If I had asked you: How many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs are at the source of the deep, or how many paths lead out above the firmament, or what are the exits of Hades, or which are the paths of paradise —

**8** perhaps you would have said: I have not gone down into the deep, nor into Hades, neither have I ever ascended into heaven.

**9** But now I have asked you about fire and wind and the day — things through which you have passed, and without which you cannot exist — and you have given me no answer about them.

**10** And he said to me: Your own things that grow up with you you are not able to know;

**11** how then can your vessel comprehend the way of the Most High? And how can one already corrupted beyond measure understand incorruption?

**12** Then I said to him: It were better that we had not come here at all, than that we should come and live in ungodliness, and suffer, and know why we suffer.

**13** And he answered me and said: Once the forests of trees went out to battle against the sea, to drive it back; and the sea likewise came to battle against the forest, to take possession of it.

**14** But the counsel of the trees was in vain, for fire came and consumed them.

**15** Likewise the counsel of the waves of the sea was also in vain, for the sand stood firm and withstood it.

**16** If you were now the judge between these two, whom would you justify, and whom would you condemn?

**17** I answered and said: Both of them had a vain counsel, for the land is given to the forest, and the place of the sea is its own to carry its waves.

**18** Then he answered me and said: You have judged well, and why have you not judged so for yourself also?

**19** For as the land is given to the forest and the sea to its waves, so also they who dwell upon the earth can understand only earthly things, and those who are above the heavens can understand only the things that are above the height of the heavens.

**20** Then I answered and said: I beseech you, my lord, why then was I given the power to understand?

**21** For I had no desire to inquire about the ways of the Most High or to search out the deep; I desired only to know the things that pass before us daily:

**22** why Israel has been given over to the Gentiles as a reproach; why the people whom you loved have been handed over to godless tribes; why the law of our fathers has been made of no effect; and why the written covenants are nowhere to be found;

**23** why we have passed away from the world like locusts, and our life is like a vapor, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.

**24** But what will he do for his name that is called over us? It is about these things that I have asked.

**25** Then he answered me and said: If you live long enough you will be amazed, for the age is hastening swiftly to its end.

**26** It is unable to hold the things promised to the righteous in the appointed times, for this age is full of grief and infirmities.

**27** For the evil sown in it has not yet borne all its fruit, and the field that contains the evil seed has not yet come to its full harvest.

**28** For the grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning — how much ungodliness has it brought forth until now, and how much more shall it bring forth until the time of threshing comes!

**29** Consider now for yourself how great a harvest of ungodliness has ripened;

**30** when shall the field of good seed be cut for harvest, unless it be after the time I speak of?

**31** I answered and said: How long and when will these things be? For our years are few and evil.

**32** And he answered me and said: Do not hurry more than the Most High; for you hasten only for yourself, but the Most High hastens for many.

**33** Were not the souls of the righteous asking in their chambers these very things: How long must we remain here? When comes the fruit of the threshing-floor of our reward?

**34** And to these the archangel Jeremiel answered: Not until the full number of those like you is complete; for he has weighed the age in a balance,

**35** and measured the times by measure, and numbered the seasons by number; and he will not stir nor rouse them until the appointed measure is fulfilled.

**36** Then I answered and said: O LORD who art above us, if even we who dwell on the earth know all this, how much more do you know it.

**37** As a pregnant woman in the ninth month, when the hour of her delivery draws near, feels her womb ache, so also shall these places be — they shall not hesitate one moment beyond what is appointed.

**38** Then I answered and said: If I have found grace before you, and if it is possible, and if I am worthy,

**39** show me this also: whether more time is still to come than has already passed, or whether the greater part has gone by.

**40** I have heard the things that are past, but I do not know the things that are to come.

**41** And he said to me: Stand at my right hand and I will show you the meaning of a parable.

**42** And I stood and saw: a burning furnace passed before me, and when the flame had passed by I looked, and behold, the smoke still remained.

**43** And after that a cloud full of water passed before me, and after the heavy rain had fallen there were still drops remaining in the cloud.

**44** And he said to me: Consider — as the rain exceeds the drops, and the fire exceeds the smoke, so the quantity that has passed exceeded what remains; but the drops and the smoke are still there.

**45** Then I prayed and said: Do I think I shall live until those days? Or who will be alive in those days?

**46** He answered me and said: Concerning the signs about which you ask me, I am able to tell you in part; but concerning your life I have not been sent to tell you, and I do not know.
